clue.text: Smiled wryly when deceived

indicators.note: done wryly, the word is twisted out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gave a crooked smile on discovering they had been fooled.
explanation.definitionFit: To be deceived is to be led astray by false information.

clue.text: Spy boss with dissolute person it's a plant!

parts.note: M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories
with is another way of saying and
a rake is a debauched, dissolute man

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the spymaster and a libertine turn out to be a plant, as in an infiltrator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a planted spy in this espionage surface, but it is the herb, a poisonous root of folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandrake is a Mediterranean herb with a forked root, long linked to magic.

clue.text: Give voice about a market that's causing some distress

indicators.note: about means the singing word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to give voice is to sing
a mart is a market

explanation.surface: Shouting out around a market causes some upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' tells you to wrap the singing word round the other two pieces; 'causing some distress' describes a sting, not a shopping trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarting describes a sharp stinging pain, a kind of distress.

clue.text: There's need for variety in the garden

indicators.note: for variety means the letters are mixed into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A gardener wants more variety in the planting.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, the first humans lived in a paradise garden.

clue.text: The woman laid in a river

indicators.note: in means the word laid is placed inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and also one on the England-Wales border

explanation.surface: A woman was laid down in the water, perhaps at a baptism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The woman' looks like the subject of a sentence, but it defines a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide is a female first name, so it names a particular woman.

clue.text: Marking time

parts.note: read as waiting idly, but literally the act of stamping a date on documents

explanation.definitionFit: Applying a rubber stamp with the day's date marks the time on a document.

clue.text: Christmas all upset and by oneself

indicators.note: all upset means the letters are tipped over into a new order

parts.note: Noel is another word for Christmas

explanation.surface: Someone feels upset and alone at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alone means being without company, solitary.

clue.text: Not an upright type

parts.note: sounds like a dishonest person, but refers to printing type that slopes

explanation.definitionFit: Sloping print, as opposed to upright roman, is the typeface style named after Italy.

clue.text: Points to what's owing for clothes

parts.note: E and N are two compass points, east and north
dues are sums owed

explanation.surface: Someone indicates what money is owed for some garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' reads as a noun, but it is the verb, to dress or endow.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue is to dress or invest someone, as with a robe or quality.

clue.text: \Mid-evening diner — it's more elegant

indicators.note: mid points to the central letter of the word evening

parts.note: a diner is someone who eats, an eater

explanation.surface: A guest dining in the middle of the evening is the smarter one.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of the seven-letter EVENING is N.
explanation.definitionFit: Neater means tidier, smarter in appearance.

clue.text: Flag, as usual

explanation.surface: A banner flown in the customary way.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a banner carried as an emblem; standard also means normal, customary.

clue.text: Hearty but cute — this is an anomaly

indicators.note: an anomaly is something out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something warm but sweet is an oddity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anomaly' rearranges the letters of CUTE THIS IS AN; 'but' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearty welcome is a keen, wholehearted one.

clue.text: Estimate speed

explanation.surface: Judging how fast something goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate is to assess or value; a rate is also a pace or velocity.

clue.text: Snap together that which hangs loosely

indicators.note: loosely means the letters are set free from their order

explanation.surface: Clicking shut something that dangles slackly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snap together' means grinding or clashing the teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Grinding or clashing the teeth together, often in anger.

clue.text: Splendid as 30 across can be

explanation.surface: Something excellent, as a prison term may be.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine means excellent; a monetary penalty is a kind of judicial punishment, as 30 across is.

clue.text: Pause or pass on

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: Stop or hand something on.
explanation.walkthrough: A COL is a gap between two peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation mark marks a pause in a sentence, longer than a comma.

clue.text: The seaman in an ocean-going vessel called for night lights

indicators.note: in means the sailor goes inside the ship's letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor aboard ship calls for lamps at night.
explanation.definitionFit: The points of light in the dark sky are distant suns.

clue.text: Asking for the wrong card

indicators.note: wrong means the letters are set out in an incorrect order

explanation.surface: Requesting the wrong card in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A playing card, the highest court card in the red suit with the heart symbol.

clue.text: A flier's restricted accommodation

parts.note: suggests a pilot's cramped lodging, but describes the cage where a pet bird is kept

explanation.definitionFit: A wire cage confines a pet bird, which is a flying creature.

clue.text: A desert's to be put to good use, it's claimed

indicators.note: put to good use means the letters are reorganised into something useful

parts.note: the letters of desert's, taken with its S

explanation.surface: Someone claims a desert is to be cultivated productively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put to good use' rearranges DESERTS, the apostrophe ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert something is to state or maintain it firmly.

clue.text: Overnight guests of Tory, Alliance and Labour politicians?

definitions.text: Overnight guests of Tory, Alliance and Labour politicians?

parts.words: Overnight guests of Tory, Alliance and Labour politicians?
parts.note: the political parties represented in the House of Commons, read as social gatherings at a country house

explanation.walkthrough: The Alliance was a 1980s grouping of Liberals and Social Democrats in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Gatherings where guests stay several nights at a country home.

clue.text: They're up for approval

parts.note: sounds like candidates being considered, but describes digits raised as a sign of approval

explanation.definitionFit: Raising the digits upward is a gesture of approval.

clue.text: Annoy a cleric when other people are around

indicators.note: around means the other people surround the rest

parts.note: men stands for people in general
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a cleric's degree

explanation.surface: Someone irritates a clergyman when others are present.
explanation.definitionFit: To madden is to irritate intensely, drive someone mad.

clue.text: The man a trainee put right

parts.note: he refers to a man
L is a learner, as on British L-plates for learner drivers

explanation.surface: A man and a beginner fixed something.
explanation.definitionFit: To heal is to cure, restore to health.

clue.text: Chase around a favourite resort

indicators.note: around means the chasing word goes round the letter a

parts.note: to hunt is to chase

explanation.surface: Pursuing someone around a popular holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A haunt is a place one frequents often.

clue.text: Move carefully among the aged getting frail

indicators.note: among means the answer sits within the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Moving cautiously among the old people as they grow weak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frail' completes the picture of the elderly and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge is to inch forward slowly and cautiously.

clue.text: Pen a note making complaint

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Writing a letter of complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' is not writing but an enclosure, and 'complaint' is a medical ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can be a minor ailment, like a swelling on the eyelid.

clue.text: Give up from choice, deliberate choice

indicators.note: from means the answer is drawn out of the letters of the next words

explanation.surface: Surrendering freely, as a considered decision.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans choiCE DEliberate; the final 'choice' completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to surrender or hand over.

clue.text: Think time and date should be changed

indicators.note: should be changed means the letters of the two words are reordered

explanation.surface: Considering that an appointment needs rescheduling.
explanation.definitionFit: To meditate is to reflect or contemplate deeply.

clue.text: The meal's about over

parts.note: re means about, concerning
past means over, finished

explanation.surface: Dinner is nearly finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a meal, a formal word for one.

clue.text: 14 across this may be, but it must come to a stop

definitions.text: it must come to a stop

explanation.surface: A punishment that may be fine, but must end.
explanation.walkthrough: A judicial sentence can be a fine; a written sentence ends with a full stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A court's punishment, which may be a fine; also a grammatical unit ending in a full stop.

clue.text: Such a story makes a member object

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: A tale that makes a club member protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a traditional tale passed down.
